Level 4 · Agentic AI

Level 4: Agentic AI Architecture

Design systems where AI agents do real work: tools, memory, limits, evaluation and human approval, documented so the next engineer can trust them.

Open the courseSee pathways

Live online course US$249

Who it is for
Architects and engineers who add agents to products or run agents inside their organisation.
Before you start
Level 3, Quality, Decisions and Evaluation, or equivalent experience designing systems against quality goals.
Capstone evidence
One agent system design: tools as contracts, memory, limits, human approval, rules an agent must follow with the checks that enforce them, and an evaluation plan.
How it is assessed
Quiz questions in every lesson and a lab with health checks across 16 sections, including a check that every rule names the test or reviewer that verifies it. The certificate shows you finished the course.

Modules and evidence

Each module ends in an artefact that goes into your record.

ModuleWhat it coversEvidence
Agents as componentsWhat an agent is, architecturally.A workflow-or-agent decision with reasons, tool contracts and an autonomy level
Deciding with AIUse AI to widen your options without handing over the decision.A decision tested as a hypothesis, with an AI-assisted option comparison and its review points
Knowledge and control for coding agentsMake the architecture something an agent can read and cannot quietly break.Machine-readable architecture rules, each with the check that verifies it or a named human reviewer
Running agent systems you can trustPatterns, limits, evidence and responsibility.Orchestration, approval and failure design with budgets, an evaluation plan, tracing design and an agent architecture document

External mapping

Related published material, as references and optional pathways only.

Reference or frameworkHow we use it
Cybersecurity for Agentic Environments AcademyThe security side of agent systems is taught there. Level 4 here is about design; the two are meant to be taken together.
iSAQB CPSA-A module AGENTAThe public curriculum (2026.1-rev5, 31 July 2026) was read on 27 November 2026: seven sections and 34 learning goals. The lessons are written against those topics. This is a topic benchmark only: no iSAQB credit is offered and Intellica is not an accredited provider.

Level 4 is independent self-study. It is not iSAQB AGENTA training and gives no iSAQB credit. Research it cites is recent, mostly preprints, and its limits are stated in each lesson.
